help.intro: Two short street scenes of about two minutes in all: a tourist in Heidelberg asks the way to the castle, gets a long answer and a tip about the funicular; then a man asks a woman for the station and finds out that the bus is faster than walking. The scenes are invented; the places in Heidelberg are real. You hear what you have just learnt: asking the way (Wie komme ich zum …? Können Sie mir helfen?), the directions (geradeaus, links, rechts, die zweite Straße, bis zur Kreuzung, gegenüber, an der Ampel) and the dative pronouns (mir, Ihnen, ihm, ihr: Ich zeige es Ihnen. Das hilft mir). Listen once for each scene as a whole, then once for the turns.
help.tips[0].title: Directions
help.tips[0].text: geradeaus (straight on), links / rechts (left / right), nach links abbiegen (turn left), die erste / zweite Straße rechts, bis zur Kreuzung (to the crossroads), bis zur Ampel (to the traffic lights), über die Brücke (over the bridge), an der Kirche vorbei (past the church), gegenüber (opposite), neben, hinter, auf der linken Seite. Distances: fünf Minuten zu Fuß, zwei Haltestellen, zweihundert Meter. Asking: Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof / zur Altstadt / zum Schloss? Ist es weit?
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Go straight on to the crossroads, then left, and the castle is on the right-hand side.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Take the second street on the right and go past the church; the station is opposite.
help.tips[0].check.why: abbiegen = to turn; geradeaus = straight; vorbei = past.
help.tips[1].text: Some verbs take the person in the dative: helfen (Können Sie mir helfen?), zeigen (Ich zeige es Ihnen), sagen (Sagen Sie mir …), danken (Ich danke Ihnen), gefallen (Heidelberg gefällt mir), gehören, glauben. Forms: ich → mir, du → dir, er → ihm, sie → ihr, Sie → Ihnen, wir → uns, ihr → euch. Also after dative prepositions: mit mir, bei ihr, zu ihm.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Excuse me, can you help me? Of course, I will show it to you on the map.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Ask the man there, the café belongs to him. He will tell you exactly.
help.tips[1].check.q: Vielen Dank, Sie haben ____ sehr geholfen. (ich)
help.tips[1].check.why: helfen takes the dative: Sie haben mir geholfen.
help.remember[0]: geradeaus, links, rechts, bis zur Kreuzung, an … vorbei, gegenüber; Wie komme ich zum / zur …?
help.remember[1]: helfen, zeigen, sagen, danken, gefallen + dative: mir, dir, ihm, ihr, Ihnen.
help.exam: Short street scenes in which someone asks the way and gets directions are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Straight on, second left, past the church, or just take the funicular: listen to two people asking the way in Heidelberg.
passageTranslation:
Tourist: Excuse me, can you help me? How do I get to the castle?
Man: To the castle? Gladly. You go straight on here, along the Hauptstraße, about ten minutes. Then you come to the market square with the big church.
Tourist: To the market square, good.
Man: At the market square you go past the church and then right into Burgstraße. The street goes up the hill, to the castle. That takes another twenty minutes, and it is steep.
Tourist: Oh. Thirty minutes and a hill.
Man: I will give you a tip: at the Kornmarkt, right next to the market square, is the funicular. It goes up to the castle every ten minutes, in two minutes. The ticket costs nine euros, and entry to the castle is included.
Tourist: That is great. So: straight on to the market square, then to the Kornmarkt, and by funicular.
Man: Exactly. And from the top you see the whole town and the river. You will certainly like that.
Tourist: Thank you very much, you have helped me a lot!
Man: You are welcome. Have a nice day!
Man: Excuse me, I have a question. Is the main station far from here?
Woman: On foot, yes, about forty minutes. The station is not in the old town.
Man: Forty minutes? My train leaves in half an hour.
Woman: Then take the bus. The stop is over there opposite, in front of the pharmacy. Line 33 goes directly to the station, twelve minutes.
Man: Line 33, opposite in front of the pharmacy. Where do I buy the ticket?
Woman: On the bus, from the driver. Or with your phone. Two euros.
Man: Thank you! You have saved my day.
Woman: Quick, here it comes already!
